# Insights - COPA-DATA filler M7 (generated by analysis/run_analysis.py)

All numbers below are computed from `data/txt/*.TXT`; re-run the script to reproduce them.

## Data
- **Export 1 (cyclic 3 s)**: 29.10.2026 06:50:00 -> 04.11.2026 15:00:00 (6.34 days), 182,576 cyclic samples per variable, 82 INVALID timestamps, 92 orders (incl. partial first/last).
- **Export 2 (cyclic 10 s)**: 04.11.2026 15:00:00 -> 20.11.2026 11:00:00 (15.83 days), 136,801 cyclic samples per variable, 272 INVALID timestamps, 223 orders (incl. partial first/last).
- The two exports do not overlap: Export 2 starts where Export 1 ends. Only Export 1 has a label from COPA-DATA (no anomalies 04.11.2026 10:50:00 - 04.11.2026 15:00:00).

## What the anomalies are (Export 1, anomaly period vs. clean window)
- Machine stops are normal operation: 'Equipment Failure' occurs 1.83/h in the anomaly period and 2.40/h in the clean window.
- Compressed air (running): clean max 31.5, anomaly-period max 38.6; compressed air (stopped): clean max 2.2, anomaly-period max 9.4.
- Power (running): clean max 10.8, anomaly-period max 12.7.
- Fill weight (running): clean range 495.1-504.6, anomaly-period range 482.4-517.7.
- Speed glitch (target 550 / speed 1100 at order end): 17 samples in the anomaly period, 1 in the clean window -> treated as a transition artefact, not scored.
- Defect rate per order: clean-window orders [4.06, 4.073] %; complete anomaly-period orders median 4.72 % (min 3.78, max 9.29).

## Frequency ranking (D1, the 'descending list' idea)
- Fill weight (running, Export 1): 320 distinct values; most frequent 500.5 = 2.68 % of rows; 208 rare values (< 1 in 10,000 rows) = 557 rows.
- Compressed air (running, Export 1): 128 distinct values; most frequent 29.7 = 2.06 % of rows; 28 rare values (< 1 in 10,000 rows) = 130 rows.
- Power (running, Export 1): 40 distinct values; most frequent 9.4 = 5.91 % of rows; 3 rare values (< 1 in 10,000 rows) = 18 rows.
- Rare-value events (rows merged within 120 s): 165 in the anomaly period, 0 in the clean window (26.8/day). Export 2: 271 events (17.1/day).

## Anomaly episodes (D2 clean envelope, merged within 5 min per type)
- A Compressed-air drift: 39 in Export 1 anomaly period (6.3/day), 95 in Export 2 (6.0/day).
- B Power drift: 35 in Export 1 anomaly period (5.7/day), 72 in Export 2 (4.6/day).
- C Fill-weight disturbance: 88 in Export 1 anomaly period (14.3/day), 222 in Export 2 (14.0/day).
- Export 2 contains the same three anomaly types, so it is not anomaly-free; COPA-DATA gave no label for it.
- Envelope = clean min-max widened by 1.0 clean standard deviation(s); the plain min-max of the 4 h window produced false alarms in a 2-fold out-of-sample test.

## Schedule: anomaly onsets repeat in a 4-hour clock cycle
- Export 1 (cyclic 3 s), A Compressed-air drift: 67 % of 39 onsets fall in the 30-min window 0:00-0:30 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Export 1 (cyclic 3 s), B Power drift: 71 % of 35 onsets fall in the 30-min window 0:30-1:00 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Export 1 (cyclic 3 s), C Fill-weight disturbance: 34 % of 88 onsets fall in the 30-min window 1:34-2:04 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Export 2 (cyclic 10 s), A Compressed-air drift: 55 % of 95 onsets fall in the 30-min window 2:19-2:49 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Export 2 (cyclic 10 s), B Power drift: 53 % of 72 onsets fall in the 30-min window 3:03-3:33 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Export 2 (cyclic 10 s), C Fill-weight disturbance: 30 % of 222 onsets fall in the 30-min window 0:10-0:40 of the cycle (uniform would be 12.5 %).
- Random noise would not cluster like this, so the episodes are injected anomalies. The phase differs by about 2.5 h between the exports; whether this comes from the restart after the INVALID outage (04.11.2026 15:00-15:45) is an open question for COPA-DATA.

## RQ1 - detectors (Export 1)
| detector | flagged rows | alarm events/h (anomaly period) | false alarms/day (clean window) | episodes detected | alarm events on an episode | median delay | median warning before drift peak |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| D1 Frequency ranking | 0.39 % | 1.11 | 0.0 | 59 % | 83 % | 0 s | 40 s |
| D2 Clean envelope | 7.21 % | 1.31 | 0.0 | 100 % | 100 % | 0 s | 342 s |
| D3 Isolation Forest | 0.94 % | 0.65 | 0.0 | 49 % | 100 % | 154 s | 176 s |

Clean window = 4.17 h, so one false alarm there = 5.8 false alarms/day. D2 false alarms are out-of-sample (2-fold split of the clean window); D2 episodes are the reference, so its detection rate is 100 % by construction.

- A Compressed-air drift: 100 % of batch episodes also found online; median extra delay 0 s.
- B Power drift: 92 % of batch episodes also found online; median extra delay 30 s.
- C Fill-weight disturbance: 96 % of batch episodes also found online; median extra delay 30 s.
- D1 model learnt on Export 1 (3 s) and streamed on Export 2 (10 s): 267 events vs. 271 when learnt on Export 2 itself (row overlap Jaccard 0.80).
